tools.name: annotation_item_get
tools.description: Get annotation item details by ID.

tools.name: annotation_item_list
tools.description: List annotation items for a project. Supports generic `filters` (status, source_type, assignee), sorting and pagination.

filters.description: Filters. Format: {"field": {"operator": "<op>", "value": <val>}}. Operators: '' (exact), 'in', 'not', 'icontains', 'startswith', 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', 'lte', 'empty', 'not_empty'. Example: {"status": {"operator": "", "value": "pending"}}. Filterable fields: status, source_type, assignee.

page_size.description: Rows per page (server default when omitted; the server enforces its own maximum).

assignee_id.description: Database ID of the user to re-assign the item to (org_member_list id).

tools.name: annotation_queue_list
tools.description: List the annotation work queue of the CURRENT user (items where assignee = the authenticated user, in the authenticated key's own project; it cannot be pointed at another project). Use for 'my annotation queue' / 'what do I need to review'. For the project-wide item list use annotation_item_list instead. RETURNS per entry: id, status, full_object (the item being annotated), and the current user's own scores.

filters.description: Filters. Format: {"field": {"operator": "<op>", "value": <val>}}. Operators: '' (exact), 'in', 'not', 'icontains', 'startswith', 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', 'lte', 'empty', 'not_empty'. Example: {"status": {"operator": "", "value": "pending"}}. Filterable fields: status, source_type.

page_size.description: Rows per page (server default when omitted; the server enforces its own maximum).

tools.name: annotation_queue_summary
tools.description: Progress statistics for the CURRENT user's annotation queue in the authenticated key's own project (no project selector). RETURNS: total_items, pending_items, completed_items. For project-wide statistics an admin should use annotation_item_list.

tools.name: api_key_customer_revoke
tools.description: Soft-revoke the explicitly selected current-project API key, then verify revoked status. Requires user_confirmation matching its current name, preserving existing revoke semantics. No plaintext key is returned.

key_id.description: Exact resource ID from current-project reads.

user_confirmation.description: Explicit destructive user confirmation; exact selected ID, except API-key revoke requires the current key name.

tools.name: api_key_get
tools.description: Get API key details by database ID. Does NOT return the key string (only available at creation).

tools.name: api_key_list
tools.description: List API keys, ordered by type (permanent first) then creation date. Omit `org` to list across every project the key can see; pass it to scope to one. Revoked keys are hidden unless you pass status='revoked', which reveals them rather than narrowing the default set.

name.description: Filter by key name (case-insensitive contains). Example: 'prod'.

status.description: Filter by key status (exact match). 'revoked' also lifts the default hide-revoked, so it shows revoked keys instead of filtering the visible set down.

created_by_email.description: Filter by the email of the user who created the key (exact match).

include_revoked.description: true lifts the default hide-revoked and shows revoked keys too.

group_by.description: Group-by field, passed to the endpoint as-is.

filters.description: Raw filter body, sent as-is; the shorthand args above win on the same key. Format: {"field": {"operator": "<op>", "value": <val>}}. Operators: '' (exact), 'in', 'not', 'icontains', 'startswith', 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', 'lte', 'empty', 'not_empty'. Keys are API_KEY_FILTERS (e.g. 'name', 'status', 'user__email').

sort_by.description: Sort field, '-' prefix for descending. Omit for the endpoint default.

page_size.description: Rows per page (server default when omitted; the server enforces its own maximum).

tools.name: api_key_metadata_update
tools.description: Edit current-project API-key name/expiry or explicit dashboard caps and verify saved state. JWT only; preserve null/zero/-1 semantics and server actor ceilings. No creation, permissions/IP changes, ownership changes or plaintext secrets.

key_id.description: Exact resource ID from current-project reads.

expiry_date.description: ISO expiry timestamp; null clears expiry.

rate_limit.description: Requests per minute; 0 blocks, null clears cap.

spending_limit.description: Monthly spend cap; 0 blocks spend, null clears cap.

tpm_rate_limit.description: Token-per-minute cap; positive finite value or null to clear. 0 is invalid.

max_usage.description: Lifetime request cap; -1 unlimited, 0 blocks requests.

tools.name: api_key_usage_list
tools.description: Get top API keys ranked by a metric. Response is {<sort_by metric>: [rows]}; with include_all_metrics=true each row has: organization_key_id, organization_key_name, number_of_requests, total_cost (USD), total_tokens, average_latency (seconds), error_count. Only keys that appear in logs for the time range. This RANKS keys by traffic — it is NOT a key listing. PROVIDER-SCOPED QUESTIONS (user names Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/etc.): you MUST pass filters={"provider_id": {"operator": "", "value": "<provider>"}}. Without this filter, the result is top keys across ALL providers — wrong answer for a provider-scoped question. The filter IS supported (see the `filters` parameter).

is_workspace_level.description: `is_workspace_level=true` with `workspace=<workspace uuid>` (or `org=<any project of the workspace>`) aggregates every project of that workspace.

start_time.description: Start time (ISO 8601). Omit to let summary_type resolve the range.

end_time.description: End time (ISO 8601). Omit to let summary_type resolve the range.

summary_type.description: Relative range preset resolved against `date`; ignored for any bound start_time / end_time sets explicitly.

timezone_offset.description: Hours of UTC minus local time.

filters.description: Filter the input population BEFORE ranking/summarizing. Shape: {"<field>": {"operator": "<op>", "value": "<val>"}}. CRITICAL: operator "" (empty string) means EXACT EQUALITY — pass it as a literal empty string, NOT a placeholder. Filterable fields and their semantics: "provider_id" — provider slug for provider-scoped questions. Canonical slugs: "anthropic", "openai", "azure_foundry", "azure_openai", "bedrock", "google_gemini_ai", "google_vertex_ai", "cohere", "deepseek", "fireworks", "groq", "mistral", "moonshot", "openrouter", "perplexity", "together_ai", "xai", "cerebras". NOTE the underscored compound forms — "google" is NOT a slug (use "google_gemini_ai" or "google_vertex_ai"); "vertex" is NOT a slug (use "google_vertex_ai"); "azure_foundry" (Azure AI Foundry) and "azure_openai" (legacy Azure OpenAI) are separate slugs — for Azure questions query both and combine. REQUIRED when the user names a specific provider; without it the tool returns a global ranking/summary across ALL providers, which is the wrong answer for provider-scoped questions. If the user says "Google" without specifying Gemini vs Vertex, ask which one or call separately for both and combine. Example: {"provider_id": {"operator": "", "value": "anthropic"}}. "model" — specific model string; used for model-name filtering, NOT provider filtering. Use operator "icontains" for model — stored names carry version/date suffixes ("gpt-5.1-2025-11-13"), so an exact match on "gpt-5.1" misses most logs. "organization_key_id" — UUID of an API key (resolve a user-given key name via api_key_list first; this field never accepts names). "customer_identifier" — end-user/customer tag string. "deployment_name" — deployment slug string. This filter IS supported on every dashboard tool whose schema exposes a `filters` parameter (the *_usage_list family, metric_timeseries, metric_summary, metric_chart_get, end_user_active_summary, metric_quantile_timeseries, metric_quantile_summary); never tell the user a tool that has this parameter cannot filter by these fields.

credential_type.description: Narrow results by who owns the credentials used for the request. 'managed' = only Respan managed keys (used_custom_credential=false); 'custom' = only customer BYOK keys (used_custom_credential=true); 'all' (default) = no filter. 'managed' and 'custom' bypass dashboard MVs and scan ch_log_v3 — slower on wide windows.

limit.description: Max results (omit for the server default).

include_all_metrics.description: Return the full metric row per item instead of only the sort_by metric (default: false).

tools.name: automation_commit
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Commit a automation family's current draft version. Flips the draft's is_read_only to True IN PLACE (same version number — unlike prompt_commit there is no auto-bump; create the next draft with automation_version_create). Takes the FAMILY automation_id (the workflow_id field from automation_list/automation_get), NOT a version PK (id). Committing does NOT make the version live — call automation_deploy next. Errors with 409 when the family has no draft to commit. RETURNS: the committed version's full details (same fields as automation_get).

version_description.description: Optional commit message stamped on the committed version.

automation_id.description: Family automation_id (UUID) — from automation_list or automation_get. NOT a version PK.

tools.name: automation_create
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. RETURNS: id (version PK), workflow_id (family ID — pass it as automation_id to automation_get / automation_update), version, name, tasks. Task types: condition (filter/gate), sampling (random %), eval (run a grader), ingest (save to dataset), webhook (HTTP callback), notification (email/Slack/PagerDuty), aggregation (time-window metrics), switch (multi-branch routing), compute (arithmetic on upstream outputs). Task ordering: gates first (condition, sampling) then aggregation then actions (notification, webhook, eval, ingest). TRIGGER MAPPING: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' to request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' to trace_completed. UI CONVENTION: tasks MUST start with a sampling task whose id is LITERALLY 'auto-sampling' (type='sampling', config.rate 0.0-1.0, default 1). The top-level 'Run workflow on X% of incoming' control is backed by that exact task id. '+ Add task' palette (what the user sees): condition (Filtering), aggregation, compute (Computation), switch, webhook, ingest (Dataset), eval (Evaluator). HIDDEN from that menu but still valid and executable: notification, prompt, completion, throttle. If you include a hidden-type task, your final message MUST state which inlined tasks are not in the '+ Add task' menu.

name.description: Workflow name — a clean descriptive title (e.g., 'Error Spike Alert'), never the user's raw request sentence.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this automation does. Workflows are always created disabled: make one live with automation_commit + automation_deploy.

trigger_event_type.description: Event type this automation is designed to handle (values: request_log, trace_completed, customer_budget_limit_reached, credit_low_balance_threshold_reached, limit_policy_soft_triggered, limit_policy_hard_triggered, on_eval_result_ingested, custom_event, eval_only, scheduled). UI wording → enum: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' → request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' → trace_completed; 'eval result' → on_eval_result_ingested. 'scheduled' (the reports trigger) fires on schedule_cron instead of an event and REQUIRES schedule_cron.

schedule_cron.description: UTC cron schedule, standard 5-field syntax (e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 09:00 UTC). REQUIRED when trigger_event_type='scheduled', rejected otherwise. No seconds field, no TZ=/CRON_TZ= prefix, minimum 5 minutes between fires. A scheduled automation only fires once a committed version is enabled.

is_starred.description: Favourite flag shown in the UI.

polarity.description: Whether a True/passing verdict is good (positive), bad (negative) or informational (neutral). Drives red/green coding and net-sentiment rollups; does NOT change scoring. Omit to keep the current value (neutral on create).

tasks.description: Ordered list of automation tasks. Chain via `next`. If type='automations', FIRST task MUST be {id:'auto-sampling', type:'sampling', label:'<pct>% sampling', config:{rate:<0-1>}, next:'<first-user-task-id>'}. Then: gates (condition, switch) → aggregation/compute → actions (webhook, ingest, eval).

id.description: Unique task id — a short slug like 'agg', 'filter_failed', 'notify', NOT a UUID. It surfaces in 'next' pointers, switch targets, state.<task_id>.* dotpaths, and notification selected_variables.

type.description: Task type: condition, sampling, eval, ingest, webhook, notification, aggregation, switch, compute, prompt, completion, throttle, get_logs, get_traces, limit_breaches, get_pulse, pulse_summarize (and the other types the server accepts; an unknown type is rejected on save). get_logs/get_traces/limit_breaches/get_pulse/pulse_summarize are REPORT building blocks — use them in type='reports' automations with trigger_event_type='scheduled'.

label.description: Human-readable label for the task (e.g., 'Cost aggregation (5m)'). Required on condition, compute, transform, ingest and eval tasks, and UNIQUE across the automation (a repeated label is rejected as a duplicate), so give every task its own.

generation_method.description: eval tasks only, required there: how the score is produced ('llm', 'code', 'human', 'predefined' or 'noop'). Sits on the task, next to type and label.

next.description: ID of the next task to execute after this one succeeds. When omitted, the server chains the task to the one after it in the array (switch branch targets are left unchained). Set it explicitly to branch or to end a chain early.

config.description: Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type: NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id — NOT label), context (project/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state. CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix: • Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc. • Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.primary_score' (eval task), etc. NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time. OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE: • Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}. • Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}. • Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}. • Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'. NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop'). Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}. SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task). EVAL → task-level generation_method: 'llm'|'code'|'human'|'predefined'|'noop' (required, a sibling of config, not inside it). config: evaluator_id: str (a GRADER id from grader_list, NOT an evaluator id), data_source, score_value_type, score_config, plus the inline config for the method — llm_config, code_config, human_config or predefined_config (noop takes none). Output: {primary_score, boolean_value, string_value, evaluator_name, evaluator_slug} — there is no 'score' key; reference primary_score (numeric) or boolean_value / string_value. INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment' (required), target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID. NOTIFICATION → notification_method_ids: [str] (UUIDs from notification_method_list) — ONE notification task carries every destination it should reach; do not chain one task per destination. Repeated IDs are merged on save. severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', selected_variables: [str] — the namespace dotpaths whose values the alert body lists. This is the ONLY field that puts data in the body. Use the same dotpaths condition_policy uses: 'event.status_code', 'event.error_message', 'event.customer_identifier', 'state.<task_id>.<output_field_name>'. Each path renders as one 'Label: value' line, labelled from the LAST dotpath segment, with values over 200 characters truncated. A path that resolves to nothing is dropped from the body silently, so name paths the automation actually produces. subject_template: str (optional) — double-brace Jinja2 over that same namespace, e.g. '{{context.automation_name}}: {{event.status_code}}'. It sets the subject line only, never the body, and a report digest overrides it with its own dated title. message_template is NOT supported. The field was removed from the notification config, nothing renders it at delivery time, and passing it is rejected here. Put the fields in selected_variables instead. BODY PRECEDENCE: a fired threshold renders a BUILT-IN body and selected_variables is not used — the metrics-and-threshold summary for a monitor that also runs a get_logs step, and the eval-alert rows for an automation. A report renders its built-in digest. selected_variables is the body whenever none of those apply, which is where a condition-only monitor with no get_logs step lands, and when it is empty or omitted there the body is the bare line '🚨 Automation <name> triggered' with no data in it. ALWAYS set selected_variables: it is harmless when a built-in body wins, and it is the only thing standing between a threshold alert and that bare line. Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}. WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}. AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}]. AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write. For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' automations, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}. SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'}. First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field. COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}. PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}. COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}. THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam. REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire): GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is project + window. GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period. LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}. GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}. PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

tools.name: automation_delete
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Delete a automation and ALL its versions permanently. DANGEROUS: Any automations referencing this automation will be invalidated. You MUST ask the user to confirm the automation name before calling this tool.

user_confirmation.description: REQUIRED: The exact automation name as typed by the user. Must match exactly.

automation_id.description: Family automation_id (UUID) — from automation_list or automation_get

tools.name: automation_deploy
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Deploy a committed automation version as the live version: sets is_enabled=True on exactly one committed (is_read_only=True) version and False on every other version in the family. This per-version is_enabled is the ONLY deployment truth — the is_enabled flag on automation_list/automation_get rows is a family-level serializer artifact; trust deployed_version instead. Takes the FAMILY automation_id (from automation_list/automation_get), NOT a version PK. 'version' is the integer version NUMBER (from automation_version_list), NOT a PK; omit it to deploy the latest committed version. Drafts are NOT auto-committed (unlike prompt_deploy) — call automation_commit first, and 404 means no committed version exists yet. Scheduled automations (reports) only start firing once deployed. RETURNS: id (version PK), workflow_id, version, is_enabled, is_read_only.

version.description: Integer version NUMBER to deploy (from automation_version_list). NOT a version PK. Must already be committed. Omit to deploy the latest committed version.

automation_id.description: Family automation_id (UUID) — from automation_list or automation_get. NOT a version PK.

tools.name: automation_eval_run_history
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Scores are matched by this automation's id, stamped on each graded row, covering every evaluator it runs. Eval run history for ONE evaluator (or one automation's online eval) — one row per graded log, newest first. RETURNS: {count, results: [{log_unique_id, run_at, eval_cost, output_primary_score, output_boolean_value, evaluator_scores: [{evaluator_family_id, evaluator_id, evaluator_name, primary_score, boolean_value, status, cost}], grader_scores: [{evaluator_id, scorer, evaluator_name, primary_score, boolean_value, status}], src_input, src_output, src_model, src_status, src_timestamp, src_trace_unique_id}]}. THREE levels, never averaged together: output_* is the single rollup score for the log; evaluator_scores is one entry per evaluator that ran on it (key columns on evaluator_family_id, which survives an evaluator commit — evaluator_id is the version and changes); grader_scores are the graders' sub-scores that fed each evaluator. eval_cost is every evaluator's cost on that log summed. status is pending / completed / failed: a failed evaluator has a row with no score, while one that never ran has no row at all, and output_* is null when every evaluator failed. Boolean values are 1 pass / 0 fail / 2 N/A. src_* fields describe the graded log and are null when it is outside retention. run_at is grading time, not the source log's timestamp. By default automation_id is an EVALUATOR's family id; pass scope=automation when it is an AUTOMATION's.

start_time.description: Start time (ISO 8601). Omit start_time/end_time to use the server's default window (the last 30 days).

summary_type.description: Preset window around `date`: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly or last_24h. start_time/end_time override it.

date.description: ISO 8601 date the summary_type window is anchored on (default: now).

timezone_offset.description: Hours UTC is ahead of the viewer's local time; shifts day boundaries and day buckets.

limit.description: Rows per page (server default and cap apply).

automation_id.description: Family automation_id (UUID) — the workflow_id field from automation_list or automation_get, NOT the version PK (id). A version PK returns an empty result rather than an error.

tools.name: automation_eval_score_summary
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Scores are matched by this automation's id, stamped on each graded row, covering every evaluator it runs. Aggregate output score for ONE evaluator (or one automation's online eval) across the whole window — a single collapsed row, no time buckets. RETURNS a one-row list: [{workflow_version_id, evaluator_id, scorer, evaluator_name, avg_primary_score, true_ratio, sample_count}]. Read avg_primary_score for numeric graders and true_ratio (fraction that passed, N/A rows excluded from the denominator) for boolean ones — the other is null. sample_count is the number of scores behind the average. An empty list means no scores in the window. The key columns come back empty by design: this is the evaluator's one output score collapsed across versions, not a per-grader breakdown. For per-grader sub-scores use automation_eval_run_history.

start_time.description: Start time (ISO 8601). Omit start_time/end_time to use the server's default window (the last 30 days).

tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. This is delivery history, not grading. For the scores this automation produced, use automation_eval_run_history. Delivery history for ONE automation — one row per run that DELIVERED a notification (an alert), newest first. This is NOT a list of executions. A row exists only for runs that fired or failed at least one notification, so a monitor that evaluates on every incoming log and stays under its threshold produces no rows at all while running constantly. Never report an empty result as 'this automation never ran', and never report the row count as a run count — it counts alerts. RETURNS: {count, results: [{unique_id, timestamp, workflow_version_id, workflow_version_type, workflow_status (completed | stopped | failed), delivery_fired_count, delivery_failed_count}]}. Delivery counts are the notification methods that fired or errored on that run. Rows are also forward-only: only runs executed after the executor began writing them appear, so an older automation can return an empty history despite having alerted.

tools.name: automation_undeploy
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Undeploy a automation: sets is_enabled=False on EVERY version in the family, so the automation stops firing. Exact inverse of automation_deploy — re-enable by calling automation_deploy again. This is the ONLY way to disable a automation short of deleting it. Per-version is_enabled is the ONLY deployment truth, and the is_enabled field on automation_update is IGNORED by the server (read-only there), so no update call can stop a firing automation. The is_enabled on automation_list/automation_get rows is a family-level serializer artifact; confirm the result with deployed_version instead. Takes the FAMILY automation_id (from automation_list/automation_get), NOT a version PK. There is no version argument — undeploy is family-wide by definition. Already-undeployed families succeed unchanged; 404 means no such family. Nothing is deleted: versions, tasks and run history all survive. RETURNS: nothing but the success envelope: the endpoint replies 204 No Content with an empty body.

tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. Update this automation. Edits land on the family's draft version; when every version is already committed this forks a new draft automatically and applies the edit there, so no separate version_create call is needed. RETURNS: updated automation details (same fields as automation_get). When a new draft was forked the response also carries version, is_live=false and a message — a forked draft changes nothing that is running until you commit and then deploy it. When updating tasks, the entire task list is REPLACED — provide the full task list, not just the changed tasks. Omitted fields stay unchanged.

trigger_event_type.description: Update the event type this automation handles (values: request_log, trace_completed, customer_budget_limit_reached, credit_low_balance_threshold_reached, limit_policy_soft_triggered, limit_policy_hard_triggered, on_eval_result_ingested, custom_event, eval_only, scheduled). tasks.description: Replacement task list (replaces ALL existing tasks).

id.description: Unique task id — a short slug like 'agg', 'filter_failed', 'notify', NOT a UUID. It surfaces in 'next' pointers, switch targets, state.<task_id>.* dotpaths, and notification selected_variables.

type.description: Task type: condition, sampling, eval, ingest, webhook, notification, aggregation, switch, compute, prompt, completion, throttle, get_logs, get_traces, limit_breaches, get_pulse, pulse_summarize (and the other types the server accepts; an unknown type is rejected on save). get_logs/get_traces/limit_breaches/get_pulse/pulse_summarize are REPORT building blocks — use them in type='reports' automations with trigger_event_type='scheduled'.

label.description: Human-readable label for the task (e.g., 'Cost aggregation (5m)'). Required on condition, compute, transform, ingest and eval tasks, and UNIQUE across the automation (a repeated label is rejected as a duplicate), so give every task its own.

generation_method.description: eval tasks only, required there: how the score is produced ('llm', 'code', 'human', 'predefined' or 'noop'). Sits on the task, next to type and label.

next.description: ID of the next task to execute after this one succeeds. When omitted, the server chains the task to the one after it in the array (switch branch targets are left unchained). Set it explicitly to branch or to end a chain early.

config.description: Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type: NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id — NOT label), context (project/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state. CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix: • Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc. • Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.primary_score' (eval task), etc. NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time. OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE: • Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}. • Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}. • Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}. • Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'. NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop'). Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}. SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task). EVAL → task-level generation_method: 'llm'|'code'|'human'|'predefined'|'noop' (required, a sibling of config, not inside it). config: evaluator_id: str (a GRADER id from grader_list, NOT an evaluator id), data_source, score_value_type, score_config, plus the inline config for the method — llm_config, code_config, human_config or predefined_config (noop takes none). Output: {primary_score, boolean_value, string_value, evaluator_name, evaluator_slug} — there is no 'score' key; reference primary_score (numeric) or boolean_value / string_value. INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment' (required), target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID. NOTIFICATION → notification_method_ids: [str] (UUIDs from notification_method_list) — ONE notification task carries every destination it should reach; do not chain one task per destination. Repeated IDs are merged on save. severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', selected_variables: [str] — the namespace dotpaths whose values the alert body lists. This is the ONLY field that puts data in the body. Use the same dotpaths condition_policy uses: 'event.status_code', 'event.error_message', 'event.customer_identifier', 'state.<task_id>.<output_field_name>'. Each path renders as one 'Label: value' line, labelled from the LAST dotpath segment, with values over 200 characters truncated. A path that resolves to nothing is dropped from the body silently, so name paths the automation actually produces. subject_template: str (optional) — double-brace Jinja2 over that same namespace, e.g. '{{context.automation_name}}: {{event.status_code}}'. It sets the subject line only, never the body, and a report digest overrides it with its own dated title. message_template is NOT supported. The field was removed from the notification config, nothing renders it at delivery time, and passing it is rejected here. Put the fields in selected_variables instead. BODY PRECEDENCE: a fired threshold renders a BUILT-IN body and selected_variables is not used — the metrics-and-threshold summary for a monitor that also runs a get_logs step, and the eval-alert rows for an automation. A report renders its built-in digest. selected_variables is the body whenever none of those apply, which is where a condition-only monitor with no get_logs step lands, and when it is empty or omitted there the body is the bare line '🚨 Automation <name> triggered' with no data in it. ALWAYS set selected_variables: it is harmless when a built-in body wins, and it is the only thing standing between a threshold alert and that bare line. Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}. WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}. AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}]. AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write. For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' automations, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}. SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'}. First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field. COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}. PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}. COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}. THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam. REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire): GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is project + window. GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period. LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}. GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}. PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

Every key you pass is sent as-is, including null/empty values, so a field can be cleared; omit a key to leave it unchanged. After editing: grader_run to test the DRAFT as '<grader_id>:<draft version>' (the is_read_only=false row of grader_version_list; a bare grader_id runs the latest COMMITTED version, not your edit), then grader_commit to snapshot.

tools.name: monitor_commit
tools.description: A monitor watches incoming telemetry and alerts when a condition trips. This is the data on the Monitors page. Commit a monitor family's current draft version. Flips the draft's is_read_only to True IN PLACE (same version number — unlike prompt_commit there is no auto-bump; create the next draft with monitor_version_create). Takes the FAMILY monitor_id (the workflow_id field from monitor_list/monitor_get), NOT a version PK (id). Committing does NOT make the version live — call monitor_deploy next. Errors with 409 when the family has no draft to commit. RETURNS: the committed version's full details (same fields as monitor_get).

version_description.description: Optional commit message stamped on the committed version.

monitor_id.description: Family monitor_id (UUID) — from monitor_list or monitor_get. NOT a version PK.

tools.name: monitor_create
tools.description: A monitor watches incoming telemetry and alerts when a condition trips. This is the data on the Monitors page. RETURNS: id (version PK), workflow_id (family ID — pass it as monitor_id to monitor_get / monitor_update), version, name, tasks. Task types: condition (filter/gate), sampling (random %), eval (run a grader), ingest (save to dataset), webhook (HTTP callback), notification (email/Slack/PagerDuty), aggregation (time-window metrics), switch (multi-branch routing), compute (arithmetic on upstream outputs). Task ordering: gates first (condition, sampling) then aggregation then actions (notification, webhook, eval, ingest). TRIGGER MAPPING: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' to request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' to trace_completed. Monitors alert; they do not grade. To attach a grader, build an automation instead (automation_create).

name.description: Workflow name — a clean descriptive title (e.g., 'Error Spike Alert'), never the user's raw request sentence.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this monitor does. Workflows are always created disabled: make one live with monitor_commit + monitor_deploy.

trigger_event_type.description: Event type this monitor is designed to handle (values: request_log, trace_completed, customer_budget_limit_reached, credit_low_balance_threshold_reached, limit_policy_soft_triggered, limit_policy_hard_triggered, on_eval_result_ingested, custom_event, eval_only, scheduled). UI wording → enum: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' → request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' → trace_completed; 'eval result' → on_eval_result_ingested. 'scheduled' (the reports trigger) fires on schedule_cron instead of an event and REQUIRES schedule_cron.

schedule_cron.description: UTC cron schedule, standard 5-field syntax (e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 09:00 UTC). REQUIRED when trigger_event_type='scheduled', rejected otherwise. No seconds field, no TZ=/CRON_TZ= prefix, minimum 5 minutes between fires. A scheduled monitor only fires once a committed version is enabled.

is_starred.description: Favourite flag shown in the UI.

polarity.description: Whether a True/passing verdict is good (positive), bad (negative) or informational (neutral). Drives red/green coding and net-sentiment rollups; does NOT change scoring. Omit to keep the current value (neutral on create).

tasks.description: Ordered list of monitor tasks. Chain via `next`. If type='automations', FIRST task MUST be {id:'auto-sampling', type:'sampling', label:'<pct>% sampling', config:{rate:<0-1>}, next:'<first-user-task-id>'}. Then: gates (condition, switch) → aggregation/compute → actions (webhook, ingest, eval).

id.description: Unique task id — a short slug like 'agg', 'filter_failed', 'notify', NOT a UUID. It surfaces in 'next' pointers, switch targets, state.<task_id>.* dotpaths, and notification selected_variables.

type.description: Task type: condition, sampling, eval, ingest, webhook, notification, aggregation, switch, compute, prompt, completion, throttle, get_logs, get_traces, limit_breaches, get_pulse, pulse_summarize (and the other types the server accepts; an unknown type is rejected on save). get_logs/get_traces/limit_breaches/get_pulse/pulse_summarize are REPORT building blocks — use them in type='reports' monitors with trigger_event_type='scheduled'.

label.description: Human-readable label for the task (e.g., 'Cost aggregation (5m)'). Required on condition, compute, transform, ingest and eval tasks, and UNIQUE across the monitor (a repeated label is rejected as a duplicate), so give every task its own.

generation_method.description: eval tasks only, required there: how the score is produced ('llm', 'code', 'human', 'predefined' or 'noop'). Sits on the task, next to type and label.

next.description: ID of the next task to execute after this one succeeds. When omitted, the server chains the task to the one after it in the array (switch branch targets are left unchained). Set it explicitly to branch or to end a chain early.

config.description: Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type: NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id — NOT label), context (project/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state. CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix: • Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc. • Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.primary_score' (eval task), etc. NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time. OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE: • Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}. • Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}. • Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}. • Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'. NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop'). Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}. SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task). EVAL → task-level generation_method: 'llm'|'code'|'human'|'predefined'|'noop' (required, a sibling of config, not inside it). config: evaluator_id: str (a GRADER id from grader_list, NOT an evaluator id), data_source, score_value_type, score_config, plus the inline config for the method — llm_config, code_config, human_config or predefined_config (noop takes none). Output: {primary_score, boolean_value, string_value, evaluator_name, evaluator_slug} — there is no 'score' key; reference primary_score (numeric) or boolean_value / string_value. INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment' (required), target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID. NOTIFICATION → notification_method_ids: [str] (UUIDs from notification_method_list) — ONE notification task carries every destination it should reach; do not chain one task per destination. Repeated IDs are merged on save. severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', selected_variables: [str] — the namespace dotpaths whose values the alert body lists. This is the ONLY field that puts data in the body. Use the same dotpaths condition_policy uses: 'event.status_code', 'event.error_message', 'event.customer_identifier', 'state.<task_id>.<output_field_name>'. Each path renders as one 'Label: value' line, labelled from the LAST dotpath segment, with values over 200 characters truncated. A path that resolves to nothing is dropped from the body silently, so name paths the monitor actually produces. subject_template: str (optional) — double-brace Jinja2 over that same namespace, e.g. '{{context.automation_name}}: {{event.status_code}}'. It sets the subject line only, never the body, and a report digest overrides it with its own dated title. message_template is NOT supported. The field was removed from the notification config, nothing renders it at delivery time, and passing it is rejected here. Put the fields in selected_variables instead. BODY PRECEDENCE: a fired threshold renders a BUILT-IN body and selected_variables is not used — the metrics-and-threshold summary for a monitor that also runs a get_logs step, and the eval-alert rows for an automation. A report renders its built-in digest. selected_variables is the body whenever none of those apply, which is where a condition-only monitor with no get_logs step lands, and when it is empty or omitted there the body is the bare line '🚨 Automation <name> triggered' with no data in it. ALWAYS set selected_variables: it is harmless when a built-in body wins, and it is the only thing standing between a threshold alert and that bare line. Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}. WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}. tools.description: A report is a scheduled digest assembled from logs, traces, limit breaches and pulses. This is the data on the Reports page. Commit a report family's current draft version. Flips the draft's is_read_only to True IN PLACE (same version number — unlike prompt_commit there is no auto-bump; create the next draft with report_version_create). Takes the FAMILY report_id (the workflow_id field from report_list/report_get), NOT a version PK (id). Committing does NOT make the version live — call report_deploy next. tools.name: report_create
tools.description: A report is a scheduled digest assembled from logs, traces, limit breaches and pulses. This is the data on the Reports page. RETURNS: id (version PK), workflow_id (family ID — pass it as report_id to report_get / report_update), version, name, tasks. Task types: condition (filter/gate), sampling (random %), eval (run a grader), ingest (save to dataset), webhook (HTTP callback), notification (email/Slack/PagerDuty), aggregation (time-window metrics), switch (multi-branch routing), compute (arithmetic on upstream outputs). Task ordering: gates first (condition, sampling) then aggregation then actions (notification, webhook, eval, ingest). TRIGGER MAPPING: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' to request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' to trace_completed. Report-only task types: get_logs, get_traces, limit_breaches, get_pulse, pulse_summarize. A project has at most one report: when one exists, report_create returns it unchanged (HTTP 200) instead of creating another — use report_update to change it.

name.description: Workflow name — a clean descriptive title (e.g., 'Error Spike Alert'), never the user's raw request sentence.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this report does. Workflows are always created disabled: make one live with report_commit + report_deploy.

trigger_event_type.description: Event type this report is designed to handle (values: request_log, trace_completed, customer_budget_limit_reached, credit_low_balance_threshold_reached, limit_policy_soft_triggered, limit_policy_hard_triggered, on_eval_result_ingested, custom_event, eval_only, scheduled). UI wording → enum: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' → request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' → trace_completed; 'eval result' → on_eval_result_ingested. 'scheduled' (the reports trigger) fires on schedule_cron instead of an event and REQUIRES schedule_cron.

schedule_cron.description: UTC cron schedule, standard 5-field syntax (e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 09:00 UTC). REQUIRED when trigger_event_type='scheduled', rejected otherwise. No seconds field, no TZ=/CRON_TZ= prefix, minimum 5 minutes between fires. A scheduled report only fires once a committed version is enabled.

If type='automations', FIRST task MUST be {id:'auto-sampling', type:'sampling', label:'<pct>% sampling', config:{rate:<0-1>}, next:'<first-user-task-id>'}. AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}]. AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write. For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' reports, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}. SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'}. First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field. COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}. PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}. COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}. THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam. REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire): GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is project + window. GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period. LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}. GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}. PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

tools.name: thread_list
tools.description: List conversation threads (PAGINATED). A thread groups all logs sharing the same `thread_identifier` value. Use for: browsing recent threads, finding thread_identifier values for thread_get follow-up, or filtering threads by cost/log_count. For counting or aggregate stats across threads (total threads, total cost across all threads), use thread_summary instead. Filter Format: {"field": {"operator": "<op>", "value": <val>}}. Operators: '' (exact), 'in', 'not', 'icontains', 'startswith', 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', 'lte', 'empty', 'not_empty'. Filterable fields: thread_identifier, customer_identifier, number_of_requests (numeric), total_cost (numeric), total_tokens (numeric), environment. Default time window if start_time omitted: last 1 hour. For 'today' / 'right now' / 'currently' use last 24 hours rolling.

is_workspace_level.description: `is_workspace_level=true` with `workspace=<workspace uuid>` (or `org=<any project of the workspace>`) aggregates every project of that workspace.

filters.description: Additional filters. Format: {"field": {"operator": "<op>", "value": <val>}}.
